Trier_d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e.Sub-event_summary: On 3 September, First Army reoriented eastward, with V Corps moving across VII Corps to the right, XIX and VII advancing left and center. V Corps, filling gap with Third Army, advanced through Ardennes, crossing Meuse by 5 September, facing minimal resistance. Spread thin, units moved in columns, shifting for main effort toward Pruem and Koblenz. By 8 September, planned West Wall attack; 5th Armored entered Luxembourg on 10 September, liberating capital unopposed. Gerow ordered assembly on St. Vith-Echternach line to probe West Wall, but Hodges postponed attack for ammunition, marking pursuit's end.

Givet_d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e.Sub-event_summary: On evening of 3 September, VII Corps deployed from Mons to south of Charleroi. 9th Division ordered to seize Meuse bridgehead near Dinant, faced roadblocks and strong defense, establishing bridgeheads but facing counterattacks until relieved by 3d Armored task force on 6 September, taking Dinant on 7 September. 3d Armored, delayed by gasoline at Mons, advanced to Namur by 6 September, then to Huy and Liège by 7 September, mopping up with local welcome. Advanced on Liège-Aachen axis, taking Verviers and Eupen on 9 and 11 September, noting increasing resistance and sullen populace. By end of 10 September, deployed along Malmédy-Verviers-Herve, losing contact as Germans withdrew to West Wall, ending pursuit.
